items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: He told me about that — where he’d meet these kids at these proms

ctx.x: It sure did, and it lasted. I mean that music has been out there for some 40 years now, and hit on different generations, and I think people responded to the quality and the longevity of it, and thus that kind of ovation.

Yeah. And I was also heartened and kind of amazed, because it both exhilarated Annie and me, but brought to my attention something that I try not to pay too much attention to which is age — the fact that I was entertaining three generations. People came with their © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-

grown sons and daughters and their children’s records. They all had the albums. See it was three generations looking at us: grandpa and grandma, who were the big hard core fans forty years ago; their sons, 24, 25, out of college you know with their wives; and their kids, with the albums. And I said how old does that make me? It’s amazing. It really takes your breath away. It starts you to thinking, good Lord, that’s quite something. I think that’s really interesting. Well you know Duke did that too. He told me…
